propositions.text: The claimant is a 29-year-old single male Somali citizen who arrived in Canada in 2009 and claims protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, is a 29 year old, male, single citizen of Somalia. The claimant arrived in Canada on XXXXX 2009 and claimed for protection on XXXXX 2009. He is claiming for protection because of his membership in a particular social group under section 96 of the IRPA. He is also claiming for protection because his life is at risk and he is at risk of cruel or unusual punishment or torture under section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant is a 29-year-old single Somali male who arrived in Canada in 2009 and claims protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.

propositions.text: The claimant is a member of the Darod clan and is single.
propositions.quote: The claimant is a member of the Darod clan. He is single.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant is a member of the Darod clan and is single.

propositions.text: The claimant and family lived in Somalia and were targeted by Al-Shabaab for recruitment.
propositions.quote: The claimant and his family lived in XXXXX in XXXXX Somalia. The claimant was targeted by the Al- Shabaad, the Islamic terrorist group. They wanted to recruit him into their ranks.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant and family lived in Somalia and were targeted by Al-Shabaab for recruitment.

propositions.text: In 2008 the claimant fled to Kenya and then flew to Canada.
propositions.quote: In XXXXX 2008 the claimant was able to flee to Kenya and from there he flew to Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant fled to Kenya in 2008 and then flew to Canada.

propositions.text: The claimant's identity is accepted based on his aunt's testimony and his high school diploma.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity is accepted on the basis of his aunt's testimony and his high school diploma.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's identity is accepted based on his aunt's testimony and diploma.

propositions.text: After reviewing evidence and testimony, the claimant is neither a Convention Refugee nor in need of protection; claim is rejected.
propositions.quote: After considering all the documentary evidence and oral testimony, I find that the claimant is not a Convention Refugee nor is he a person in need of protection. His claim is not accepted.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant is not a Convention Refugee nor in need of protection and rejects the claim.

propositions.text: The claimant testified straightforwardly with no contradictions; he is credible.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified in a straight forward manner. No contradictions, inconsistencies or omissions were noted. I believe his story and I find him credible.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant credible based on his straightforward testimony without contradictions.

propositions.text: Somalia is a failed state with autonomous regions and multiple armed groups vying for control; clan protection is key.
propositions.quote: Somalia is a failed state. In the north, two de facto autonomous entities exist, Somaliland in the northwest and Puntland in the northeast. In the south the de jure government of the country has only tenuous control of the capital city. Al Shabaad, an Islamic terrorist group, the various clan militias, and the government supported by Ethiopian troops vie for control. Members of minority clans are at particular risk. There is no state protection in rump Somalia, there is only clan protection.

propositions.text: The claimant is a Darod clan member from a minority group area without clan or state protection.
propositions.quote: The claimant is a member of the Darod clan - XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX. As such, he is a member of one of the XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX. The Darod - XXXXX are however are from the XXXXX of the country in what is now called XXXXX. In XXXXX in the XXXXX of the country where the claimant lived, he was a member of a minority group and was without clan protection. There was no state protection or clan protection available to the claimant.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Somalia is a failed state with clan protection only; claimant is a Darod clan member from a minority area without protection.

propositions.text: The internal flight alternative (IFA) test has two parts: risk of persecution or harm, and whether moving is objectively unreasonable.
propositions.quote: The test for an internal flight alternative has two parts. The first issue is whether there would be more than a minimal possibility of persecution (section 96) or, on a balance of probabilities, a risk to life or a risk of cruel or unusual punishment (section 97) for the claimant in the proposed IFA location. Secondly would it be objectively unreasonable for the claimant under all circumstances to move to the designated IFA.

propositions.text: Existence of a valid IFA is determinative of refugee claim; once found, other issues need not be considered.
propositions.quote: It is well-established that the existence of a valid IFA is determinative of a refugee claim. Once an IFA is found, the Court need not consider the other issues raised by an applicant on judicial review

propositions.text: The onus is on the applicant to prove persecution risk anywhere or unreasonableness of moving if IFA found.
propositions.quote: The onus of proof is on the applicant to demonstrate that he will be persecuted anywhere in his country of origin or that it is unreasonable to expect him to move if an IFA is found (see Pena v. Minister of Citizenship and Immigration, 2009 FC 616).

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the two-part IFA test and that the applicant must prove risk or unreasonableness of moving; valid IFA ends refugee claim.

propositions.text: The claimant testified he cannot live safely in Puntland because of lack of knowledge and family clan affiliations.
propositions.quote: The claimant was asked why he could not live safely in Puntland in the northeast of the country, specifically in Bosaso, the capital city. He testified that he knew nothing about that area and that his family were from the XXXXX area in the XXXXX [now under the control of Al- Shabaad]. He also pointed out that his mother is a XXXXX and that she can not live there. He also said that his mother has two other sons, one of whom is XXXXX and the other XXXXX. He said that he can't live there [in the proposed IFA].

paragraphs.summary: The court reports the claimant's testimony that he cannot live safely in Puntland due to unfamiliarity and family clan issues.

propositions.text: Objective evidence shows Darod clan would protect claimant in Puntland; clan protection remains relevant for ordinary crime.
propositions.quote: The objective evidence indicates that the Darod clan would provide the claimant protection in Puntland. "Individual security in the traditional Somali society was dependent on the clan's, i.e. the Diya group's ability to pay compensation and to defend itself in the event of attacks. This situation has not changed much in modern times, and the clan has remained the safety net of the Somali population since the collapse of the government institutions in 1991. Vulnerability and protection in Somalia are therefore closely linked to a clan's strength. However, weak clans or groups have traditionally been able to seek protection from and affiliation to the dominant clans in a specific area. The internal clan conflicts that have characterised the situation in recent years mean, however, that affiliation to a dominant clan does not necessarily provide protection (interviews in Nairobi March 2007). ... the protection aspect is composed of a number of factors, and the individual's vulnerability and potential to obtain protection and support are dependent on several conditions. Moreover, conflicts relating to scarce resources have contributed to the impairment of the mechanisms. Clan protection is still relevant, but primarily in relation to ordinary crime. With regard to the situation linked to ideological or political conditions, which according to Landinfo's interlocutors in Nairobi in June 2008 have become a key problem, clan protection is not realistic. Additionally, the current situation is characterised by random violence and grenade and bomb attacks. The violence is indiscriminate - "Your clan cannot protect you from bombs."... However, clans continue to be important in relation to where a person flees." 1

paragraphs.summary: The court states objective evidence shows Darod clan would protect claimant in Puntland, though clan protection is limited against political violence.

propositions.text: A report notes clans support men more than women; men are welcomed back due to their role and shortage of males.
propositions.quote: Another report notes that "the clan traditionally supports both men and women, but women "do not count as much as men". In this sense, men will most certainly be welcomed back into the clan regardless of how long they have been absent from Somalia because of the shortage of males and the importance of their role in the clan. However, according to another NGO source, only Somalis know the exact assistance they could obtain from their clan."2

paragraphs.summary: The court notes a report that clans support men more than women and men are welcomed back due to their role and shortage.

propositions.text: UK assessment says Somaliland and Puntland are relatively safe but admit only those with local clan affiliations; travel is feasible within Somalia.
propositions.quote: According to a UK assessment "Somaliland and Puntland, are in general relatively safe but the authorities in these regions will only admit those who originate from that territory or those who have close affiliations to the territory through clan membership. In the case of majority clan affiliates, this means those associated with the Majerteen in Puntland and the Isaaq in Somaliland. In Somaliland taxis and 4x4 vehicles can easily travel from Hargeisa, Burao, Lasanod and Garowe. The main transportation between Somaliland and South Central is by lorry. People travel by air between Mogadishu and Hargeisa."3 As well, a Dubai based airline also flies international flights into Bosaso. The UK assessment goes on to say that "given the generally lower levels of fighting and the relative ease of travel within many areas of Somalia, the risks of travel are likely to be less problematic than those considered by the AIT. It will be feasible for many to return to their home areas from Mogadishu airport as most areas are more accessible than previously. Mogadishu airport continues to function normally. ... There are scheduled air services to a number of destinations in Somalia - Mogadishu, Bosaso, Hargeisa, Berbera, Burao and Galcaiyo."4

paragraphs.summary: The court cites a UK report that Somaliland and Puntland are relatively safe and accessible for those with clan ties; travel is feasible.

propositions.text: Austrian Red Cross reports Puntland is a clan-based autonomous region with some instability but peaceful government transitions.
propositions.quote: According to the Austrian Red Cross "Puntland is a region in the north-eastern part of Somalia and declared itself an autonomous state in 1998. Puntland is less stable than Somaliland, but has carried out a peaceful transition of government and President in 2005 and 2009, and is showing signs of trying to tackle its internal security issues which include the widespread piracy along its coastline. In contrast to Somaliland, Puntland is very much a clan-based administration, primarily based on the Majerteen clan, and is thus disputing some of the territory inside Somaliland inhabited by clans that belong to the same family as the Majerteen."5

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the Austrian Red Cross reports Puntland is a clan-based autonomous region with some instability but peaceful government transitions.

propositions.text: Based on evidence and claimant's Majerteen clan membership, claimant would not face serious persecution or risk in Bosaso, Puntland, and could fly there safely.
propositions.quote: Based on the objective evidence outlined above, and given that the claimant is a member of the Majerteen clan, I do not believe that the claimant would face a serious possibility of persecution or be at risk of his life or of harm in Bosaso, Puntland. Furthermore, I find that the claimant would be able to fly to Puntland safely.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant would not face serious risk in Bosaso, Puntland, and could safely fly there due to his Majerteen clan membership.

propositions.text: The claimant is young, single, healthy; it would not be objectively unreasonable for him to move to Puntland.
propositions.quote: The claimant is a young, single and healthy male. Under all the circumstances relevant to this claimant I find that it would not be objectively unreasonable for him to go to Puntland.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds it would not be objectively unreasonable for the young, single, healthy claimant to move to Puntland.

propositions.text: The claimant is not a Convention Refugee nor in need of protection; claim is rejected.
propositions.quote: For the above noted reasons, I find that the claimant, XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, is not a Convention Refugees nor is he a person in need of protection. His claim is rejected.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the claimant is not a Convention Refugee nor in need of protection and rejects the claim.
